raw_findings.body: The account UI (i18next, which interpolates `{{0}}` as used by the sibling keys `error-invalid-length` and `error-person-name-invalid-character`) does not substitute `{0}` and does not support MessageFormat `choice`, so the user sees the literal text "Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}."
raw_findings.evidence: error-invalid-multivalued-size=Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.
raw_findings.failure_mode: End users see raw placeholder/choice markup instead of a formatted error message.
raw_findings.impact: The account UI (i18next, which interpolates `{{0}}` as used by the sibling keys `error-invalid-length` and `error-person-name-invalid-character`) does not substitute `{0}` and does not support MessageFormat `choice`, so the user sees the literal text "Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}."
raw_findings.root_cause: The Java-theme MessageFormat wording was copied into a JavaScript (i18next) message bundle that uses a different placeholder and pluralization syntax.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Keep the i18next placeholder form for this bundle (e.g. `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).`) and exempt the double-brace form in the verifier instead of rewriting the message to Java MessageFormat syntax.
raw_findings.title: Java MessageFormat choice syntax introduced into i18next account-ui bundle
raw_findings.trigger: A user profile multivalued-size validation error is returned and rendered by the account console.

raw_findings.body: The admin console uses i18next `{{n}}` interpolation (see `userNotSaved=The user has not been saved\: {{error}}` in the same file) and has no MessageFormat choice support, so the literal string with `{0}`/`{2,choice,...}` is displayed to the administrator.
raw_findings.evidence: error-invalid-multivalued-size=Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Admin console shows unformatted placeholder markup in a validation error.
raw_findings.impact: The admin console uses i18next `{{n}}` interpolation (see `userNotSaved=The user has not been saved\: {{error}}` in the same file) and has no MessageFormat choice support, so the literal string with `{0}`/`{2,choice,...}` is displayed to the administrator.
raw_findings.root_cause: Message text was aligned to the Java theme MessageFormat syntax in a bundle consumed by i18next.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Restore the i18next-compatible form for this key (e.g. `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).`) and handle the double-brace pattern in the verifier instead.
raw_findings.title: Java MessageFormat choice syntax introduced into i18next admin-ui bundle
raw_findings.trigger: An admin saves a user whose multivalued attribute violates the configured size, and the admin console renders the validation error.

raw_findings.body: The Maven build fails with a raw RuntimeException/FileNotFoundException stack trace instead of the plugin's aggregated MojoExecutionException/validation message, and the remaining files are never verified.
raw_findings.evidence: throw new RuntimeException("unable to read file " + englishFile, e);
raw_findings.failure_mode: Build aborts with an unhandled exception rather than a reported validation error.
raw_findings.impact: The Maven build fails with a raw RuntimeException/FileNotFoundException stack trace instead of the plugin's aggregated MojoExecutionException/validation message, and the remaining files are never verified.
raw_findings.root_cause: New I/O for the derived English file wraps IOException in an unchecked exception that bypasses the existing MojoExecutionException handling in `verify()`.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Declare `verifySafeHtml()` to throw MojoExecutionException (or skip the HTML check and add a descriptive entry to `messages`) when the English bundle cannot be read, instead of throwing RuntimeException.
raw_findings.title: Missing English sibling bundle aborts the build with an unchecked RuntimeException
raw_findings.trigger: The verifier runs over a translated bundle whose derived English path does not exist (e.g. a community-only theme directory, or a locale suffix the regex maps to a non-existent `_en.properties`).

raw_findings.body: `sanitized.substring(3, 1)` throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the theme-verifier Maven plugin instead of reporting the illegal HTML.
raw_findings.evidence: messages.add("Illegal HTML in key " + key + " for file " + file + ": '" + value.substring(start, value.length() - end) + "' vs. '" + sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end) + "'");
raw_findings.failure_mode: Verifier throws an unchecked exception while formatting its own error message.
raw_findings.impact: `sanitized.substring(3, 1)` throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the theme-verifier Maven plugin instead of reporting the illegal HTML.
raw_findings.root_cause: Prefix and suffix scans are computed independently without ensuring `start + end <= min(length)`.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Clamp the suffix length, e.g. `end = Math.min(end, Math.min(value.length(), sanitized.length()) - start);` before building the message.
raw_findings.title: Diff-trimming indices can produce StringIndexOutOfBoundsException in the report message
raw_findings.trigger: A value whose removed markup is surrounded by repeating text, e.g. value "xabab" sanitized to "xab": the common-prefix length (3) plus common-suffix length (2) exceeds the sanitized length (3).

raw_findings.body: The build failure text names neither the properties file nor the message key, so a contributor cannot locate the offending translation, unlike the duplicate-key and illegal-HTML messages which include the file.
raw_findings.evidence: messages.add("Didn't find anchor tag " + matcher.group() + " in original string");
raw_findings.failure_mode: Build failure output is not actionable; the unused parameter also signals dead API surface.
raw_findings.impact: The build failure text names neither the properties file nor the message key, so a contributor cannot locate the offending translation, unlike the duplicate-key and illegal-HTML messages which include the file.
raw_findings.root_cause: New diagnostic message was written without the contextual data already available in the method signature and instance state.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Include the file and key in the message, e.g. `"Didn't find anchor tag " + matcher.group() + " in original string for key " + key + " in file " + file`, which also consumes the currently unused `key` parameter.
raw_findings.title: Anchor-mismatch message omits file and key, and the `key` parameter is unused
raw_findings.trigger: Any translated bundle whose anchor tag differs from the English source; ThemeVerifierMojo concatenates all messages from all scanned files into a single MojoFailureException.

raw_findings.body: The method and its call site use a typo ("santize") that breaks searchability and diverges from the `sanitize`/`verifySafeHtml` naming used elsewhere in the class.
raw_findings.evidence: private String santizeAnchors(String key, String value, String englishValue) {
raw_findings.impact: The method and its call site use a typo ("santize") that breaks searchability and diverges from the `sanitize`/`verifySafeHtml` naming used elsewhere in the class.
raw_findings.root_cause: Typo introduced when adding the new helper method.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Rename the method (and its invocation on line 88) to `sanitizeAnchors`.
raw_findings.title: Misspelled method name `santizeAnchors`
raw_findings.trigger: Reading or searching the new sanitizer code (e.g. grepping for "sanitize").

raw_findings.body: Two OWASP PolicyFactory instances (and the `HTML_TAGS` Pattern on line 139) are constructed and the regex recompiled for every file, adding avoidable build time; the UPPER_SNAKE naming also falsely implies constants on mutable package-private fields.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Repeated expensive initialization per file plus misleading constant-style naming.
raw_findings.impact: Two OWASP PolicyFactory instances (and the `HTML_TAGS` Pattern on line 139) are constructed and the regex recompiled for every file, adding avoidable build time; the UPPER_SNAKE naming also falsely implies constants on mutable package-private fields.
raw_findings.root_cause: New shared, immutable configuration was added as per-instance mutable fields.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Declare `POLICY_SOME_HTML`, `POLICY_NO_HTML` and `HTML_TAGS` as `private static final`, matching `ANCHOR_PATTERN`.
raw_findings.title: Sanitizer policies and pattern are non-static instance fields rebuilt for every properties file
raw_findings.trigger: ThemeVerifierMojo creates a new `VerifyMessageProperties` per message file (`new VerifyMessageProperties(file).verify()`), and the themes module contains hundreds of `messages_*.properties` files.

raw_findings.body: The RTL-style exemption is silently applied to every bundle (login/admin/account), so `style="direction: rtl;"` attributes in non-email themes are no longer flagged, defeating the check.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Verification behavior depends on the developer/CI checkout directory name.
raw_findings.impact: The RTL-style exemption is silently applied to every bundle (login/admin/account), so `style="direction: rtl;"` attributes in non-email themes are no longer flagged, defeating the check.
raw_findings.root_cause: Context detection uses an unanchored substring test on the machine-dependent absolute path.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Match on a path segment instead of a raw substring, e.g. check `file.getParentFile()` chain for a directory named "email" (or use `File.separator + "email" + File.separator`).
raw_findings.title: Email-specific normalization keyed on substring of the absolute path
raw_findings.trigger: The build runs from a checkout whose absolute path contains "email" (e.g. /home/email-team/keycloak) — or, conversely, an email bundle located outside a path segment named "email".

raw_findings.body: All four tests only assert that some message is present, so a regression that flags valid translations would still pass the unit tests and only surface as a themes-module build failure.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Test suite cannot detect false-positive regressions in the HTML sanitizer check.
raw_findings.impact: All four tests only assert that some message is present, so a regression that flags valid translations would still pass the unit tests and only surface as a themes-module build failure.
raw_findings.root_cause: New verification logic was added with positive-detection tests only; no test pins the no-findings behavior.
raw_findings.suggested_fix:
Add a test using the already-added `noHtml_en.properties` fixture (and a fixture containing allowed `
`/choice patterns) asserting `MatcherAssert.assertThat(verify, Matchers.empty())`.
raw_findings.title: Missing negative test asserting a clean bundle yields no findings
raw_findings.trigger:
A future change to `normalizeValue`, `containsHtml` or the sanitizer round-trip (unescapeHtml4 / `` removal) introduces false positives on legitimate values such as `
`, `{0,choice,...}` or `CLAIM.`.

raw_findings.body: The verifier fails the build with "Illegal HTML in key ..." for markup that is valid and allowed, forcing cosmetic edits and giving contributors a misleading error message.
raw_findings.failure_mode: False-positive build failures with a misleading diagnostic for legal HTML.
raw_findings.impact: The verifier fails the build with "Illegal HTML in key ..." for markup that is valid and allowed, forcing cosmetic edits and giving contributors a misleading error message.
raw_findings.root_cause: Validity is inferred from byte-identical equality with the sanitizer's re-serialized output instead of from removed/disallowed markup.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Compare the sanitizer output against a re-serialized/normalized form of the input (or compare the set of tags/attributes) rather than raw string equality, and word the message as "HTML differs after sanitizing" when only serialization changed.
raw_findings.title: Sanitizer round-trip comparison reports formatting differences as "Illegal HTML"
raw_findings.trigger:
A translation contains allowed but differently serialized markup, e.g. `
` (which the OWASP sanitizer re-emits as `
`) — exactly the change applied across the messages_ar/ca/cs/de/el/es/fa/fi login bundles in this patch.

finding.body: `sanitized.substring(3, 1)` throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the theme-verifier Maven plugin instead of reporting the illegal HTML.
finding.evidence: messages.add("Illegal HTML in key " + key + " for file " + file + ": '" + value.substring(start, value.length() - end) + "' vs. '" + sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end) + "'");
finding.failure_mode: Verifier throws an unchecked exception while formatting its own error message.
finding.impact: `sanitized.substring(3, 1)` throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the theme-verifier Maven plugin instead of reporting the illegal HTML.
finding.root_cause: Prefix and suffix scans are computed independently without ensuring `start + end <= min(length)`.
finding.suggested_fix: Clamp the suffix length, e.g. `end = Math.min(end, Math.min(value.length(), sanitized.length()) - start);` before building the message.
finding.title: Diff-trimming indices can produce StringIndexOutOfBoundsException in the report message
finding.trigger: A value whose removed markup is surrounded by repeating text, e.g. value "xabab" sanitized to "xab": the common-prefix length (3) plus common-suffix length (2) exceeds the sanitized length (3).
finding.verifier_reason: Patch R111 shows substring operations using start and end indices computed independently. When start+end exceeds the shorter string length (e.g., value='xabab' sanitized='xab' with start=3, end=2), sanitized.substring(3, 3-2=1) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException since beginIndex > endIndex.

rejected_findings.reason: 0.750 is below 0.920: Patch R111 shows substring operations using start and end indices computed independently. When start+end exceeds the shorter string length (e.g., value='xabab' sanitized='xab' with start=3, end=2), sanitized.substring(3, 3-2=1) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException since beginIndex > endIndex.

validated_findings.title: Email-specific normalization keyed on substring of the absolute path
validated_findings.trigger: The build runs from a checkout whose absolute path contains "email" (e.g. /home/email-team/keycloak) — or, conversely, an email bundle located outside a path segment named "email".
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim that RTL exemption defeats the check for non-email themes is speculative. The condition 'file.getAbsolutePath().contains("email")' correctly identifies email bundles in normal repository structure. The hypothetical trigger of checkout path containing 'email' is unrealistic.

validated_findings.body: All four tests only assert that some message is present, so a regression that flags valid translations would still pass the unit tests and only surface as a themes-module build failure.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Test suite cannot detect false-positive regressions in the HTML sanitizer check.
validated_findings.impact: All four tests only assert that some message is present, so a regression that flags valid translations would still pass the unit tests and only surface as a themes-module build failure.
validated_findings.root_cause: New verification logic was added with positive-detection tests only; no test pins the no-findings behavior.
validated_findings.suggested_fix:
Add a test using the already-added `noHtml_en.properties` fixture (and a fixture containing allowed `
`/choice patterns) asserting `MatcherAssert.assertThat(verify, Matchers.empty())`.
validated_findings.title: Missing negative test asserting a clean bundle yields no findings
validated_findings.trigger:
A future change to `normalizeValue`, `containsHtml` or the sanitizer round-trip (unescapeHtml4 / `` removal) introduces false positives on legitimate values such as `
`, `{0,choice,...}` or `CLAIM.`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: This is a test coverage gap suggestion, not a bug in the patch. The tests do verify positive detection cases. Missing negative tests is a quality improvement suggestion, not a defect introduced by this patch.

validated_findings.body: The verifier fails the build with "Illegal HTML in key ..." for markup that is valid and allowed, forcing cosmetic edits and giving contributors a misleading error message.
validated_findings.failure_mode: False-positive build failures with a misleading diagnostic for legal HTML.
validated_findings.impact: The verifier fails the build with "Illegal HTML in key ..." for markup that is valid and allowed, forcing cosmetic edits and giving contributors a misleading error message.
validated_findings.root_cause: Validity is inferred from byte-identical equality with the sanitizer's re-serialized output instead of from removed/disallowed markup.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Compare the sanitizer output against a re-serialized/normalized form of the input (or compare the set of tags/attributes) rather than raw string equality, and word the message as "HTML differs after sanitizing" when only serialization changed.
validated_findings.title: Sanitizer round-trip comparison reports formatting differences as "Illegal HTML"
validated_findings.trigger:
A translation contains allowed but differently serialized markup, e.g. `
` (which the OWASP sanitizer re-emits as `
`) — exactly the change applied across the messages_ar/ca/cs/de/el/es/fa/fi login bundles in this patch.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim about false positives from serialization differences is speculative. The patch includes normalization steps (unescapeHtml4, comment removal) to handle known serialization differences. The br tag changes in the patch are actual content changes being made, not false positive detections.

validated_findings.body: The Lithuanian login page shows the Italian sentence "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:" while the surrounding steps (loginTotpStep2/3) remain in Lithuanian, so the instruction is unreadable for the target audience and the file's translation is silently lost.
validated_findings.evidence: loginTotpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:
validated_findings.failure_mode: User-visible localized text is rendered in the wrong language, breaking the locale contract of the messages_lt bundle.
validated_findings.impact: The Lithuanian login page shows the Italian sentence "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:" while the surrounding steps (loginTotpStep2/3) remain in Lithuanian, so the instruction is unreadable for the target audience and the file's translation is silently lost.
validated_findings.root_cause: While stripping the embedded FreeOTP/Google Play anchors for the HTML sanitizer, the replacement value was copied from an Italian resource bundle rather than being re-translated into Lithuanian.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Replace the value with the Lithuanian equivalent of the English string "Install one of the following applications on your mobile:" (e.g. "Įdiekite vieną iš šių programėlių savo mobiliajame įrenginyje:") instead of the Italian text copied from messages_it/account messages_lt.
validated_findings.title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 replaced with Italian text
validated_findings.trigger: A user with locale `lt` reaches the OTP/mobile-authenticator setup page (loginTotpStep1 is rendered by login-config-totp.ftl).
validated_findings.verifier_reason: This describes the same defect as candidate 0 - Italian text in Lithuanian bundle. Candidate 0 covers messages_lt.properties account bundle totpStep1, candidate 12 covers login bundle loginTotpStep1. Same root cause (copy-paste from Italian), same fix needed, but different files so could be separate. However, both are the same causal pattern at different sites.
